title: X Canon Factory — LSP-complete instance introspection plus a two-discipline fabrication factory (blocks + schema packages) that keeps the agent inside the WordPress block-platform canon for styling, data, and interactivity
mission: Close the gap where the agent invents: every expressive rung of the block platform (supports, global styles, block styles, variations, per-block custom CSS in global styles, block-owned stylesheets) and every backend fundamental (post types, taxonomies, meta, block bindings, REST routes) becomes (a) READABLE from the instance through the companion — an LSP-grade surface that is always current for this WP version, theme, and active block libraries — and (b) WRITABLE only through gated factory artifacts tested in a throwaway Playground before install. The agent never works outside platform canon unless canon is provably insufficient, and it cites the rung it is on.

problem_context.why: Field evidence (the Hearth & Crumb ordering build): the agent improvises exactly where the manifest goes silent. The manifest serves blocks + theme tokens only, so form styling fell off the token cliff into unstyled markup, and storage fell off the render.php-only cliff into orders-as-comments. Both failures are introspection failures first and fabrication failures second.
problem_context.canon_principle: Never invent; escalate. Styling, data, and interactivity each get an explicit ladder whose every rung is READ from the connected instance at the current fingerprint. A rung may only be skipped by citing why it cannot express the requirement. Custom CSS and custom code are the last rungs, not the first tools.
problem_context.amends: This spec amends x-companion (specs/companion-plugin.spec.json) and x-agent (specs/agent-plugin.spec.json). Those specs stay canonical for the base contract (auth, postures, TreeIR, Diagnostics, epoch). Everything here is additive; on conflict the base specs win unless this spec explicitly overrides (it overrides R4 and extends R7).
problem_context.recorded_decision: One agent plugin, one MCP server, a second skill. A separate x-agent-backend plugin was considered and rejected: a Claude Code plugin is the unit that bundles an MCP server, so a second plugin means a second server process duplicating the config chain, redaction, REST client, Playground boot, and — fatally — a second holder of epoch state. Capability gating, when wanted, is done by the companion's extend tier and/or client-side tool allowlists, not by packaging.

expression_ladder.purpose: Replaces R4's binary token rule with an ordered ladder. The agent states the rung it lands on and why each lower rung failed; that citation is a complete explanation of a styling decision.

rungs.name: block_supports
rungs.what: Attributes the block's supports expose: color/typography/spacing/layout/border presets, align, elements.

rungs.name: global_styles_and_tokens
rungs.what: DesignTokens -> theme.json settings; per-block and per-element styles in global styles (user origin).

rungs.name: registered_block_styles
rungs.what: className is-style-* registered by theme, plugins, or a factory artifact.

rungs.name: block_variations
rungs.what: Named attribute/innerBlocks presets registered server- or client-side.

rungs.name: custom_css_in_global_styles
rungs.what: Per-block or global css written into global styles (styles.css, styles.blocks[name].css) — canon's own escape hatch since WP 6.2, theme-update-safe, reviewable as data.

rungs.name: block_owned_stylesheet
rungs.what: style.css shipped inside a factory block, built exclusively on token custom properties (var(--wp--preset--*)). Owned code; last rung.

expression_ladder.rule: A designed outcome that lands on rung 5 or 6 without a cited failure of rungs 1-4 is a defect, exactly as hand-written markup is.

interfaces.version_policy: interfaces.version bumps '1' -> '2'. All manifest additions are additive; a v1 agent keeps working against a v2 companion. The agent must read interfaces_version and not request v2 sections from a v1 instance.

manifest_additions.blocks[].styles: [{name, label, source: 'theme'|'plugin'|'agent'}] from WP_Block_Styles_Registry merged with theme.json styles.blocks.
manifest_additions.blocks[].variations: [{name, title, source: 'server'|'client', attributes, innerBlocks?}] — server-registered from the block registry; client-registered captured by the harness page (wp.blocks.getBlockVariations) once per fingerprint and cached. Replaces the write-only variations_count.
manifest_additions.global_styles: {settings: merged wp_get_global_settings(), styles: merged wp_get_global_styles() including elements and per-block styles, custom_css: {global: string, blocks: map<name, string>}}.
manifest_additions.bindings: {sources: [{name, label, uses_context}] from WP_Block_Bindings_Registry, bindable_attributes: map<block_name, string[]>, registered_meta: map<object_type, [{key, type, single, show_in_rest_schema, subtype?}]>} — the agent learns WHAT can bind to WHAT, never assumes.
manifest_additions.data_model: {post_types: [{slug, label, public, show_in_rest, rest_base, supports, taxonomies, meta_keys, source: 'core'|'plugin'|'agent'}], taxonomies: [{slug, object_types, hierarchical, show_in_rest, rest_base, source}], statuses: [...]}. The WP REST API remains the exhaustive read/write surface for content in these types; the manifest only makes the model VISIBLE.
manifest_additions.features: Capability matrix read from the running instance, never inferred from version tables by the agent: {block_bindings: bool, per_block_css: bool, interactivity_api: bool, block_hooks: bool, ...} each {available, detail?}.

rest_api_additions.GET /manifest?section=: styles|variations|global_styles|bindings|data_model|features — sectioned retrieval so the fat manifest stays cheap; summary mode lists section names + counts.
rest_api_additions.POST /schema/install: Extend tier (posture-gated identically to /blocks/install). Accepts a schema-package zip (policy below). Returns {installed:{slug,version}, fingerprint, replaced_previous}. Activation registers everything on init like real plugin code — because it is real plugin code.
rest_api_additions.GET /schema/installed: [{slug, version, provides: {post_types, taxonomies, meta_keys, binding_sources, routes}}].

diagnostics_additions: E_BINDING_UNKNOWN — tree binds an attribute to an unregistered source or unregistered meta key; fix_hint names the nearest registered source.
E_BINDING_UNBINDABLE — attribute not bindable on this block per manifest.bindings.bindable_attributes.
W_STYLE_UNKNOWN — className is-style-* not present in blocks[].styles at this fingerprint.
interfaces.fingerprint_additions: The epoch hash gains: registered post types + taxonomies + meta keys, binding sources, block styles, server-registered variations, global-styles custom_css. Installing a schema package or writing per-block css MUST move the fingerprint — they change what a valid tree means. Client-captured variations are keyed by fingerprint but are not hash inputs (server-computed hash only).
interfaces.design_tokens_additions: DesignTokens schema gains optional css: {global?: string, blocks?: map<block_name, string>} compiled by /theme/tokens into global-styles custom css (rung 5's write path). Companion sanitizes with core's global-styles CSS validation; rejected properties are itemized in the response, never silently dropped.

schema_package.purpose: The backend counterpart of an agent block: how storage, taxonomies, meta, bindings, REST behavior, and an admin surface enter the instance. Dissolves the render.php-only ceiling that produced orders-as-comments.
schema_package.artifact: A plugin directory: {slug}.php registering on init (post types, taxonomies, meta with show_in_rest schemas, binding sources), routes.php (register_rest_route with explicit permission_callback + nonces for anonymous submission flows), uninstall.php (clean removal), no build step required, size < 1MB.
policy_enforced_by_companion_on_install: Registration exclusively via core APIs (register_post_type, register_taxonomy, register_post_meta, register_block_bindings_source, register_rest_route); static analysis rejects direct SQL and direct $wpdb use (422 schema_policy).
Every registered meta key MUST carry show_in_rest with a schema — REST-invisible meta is invisible to bindings and to the agent, so it is a policy error, not a style choice.
Every custom route MUST declare permission_callback (literal true only with a nonce check in the handler); capabilities mapped, never assumed.
Admin UX = the CPT's standard admin UI (show_ui, list-table columns via standard hooks). No bundled admin frameworks.
Prefix namespace agent/{slug} mirroring agent blocks; uninstall.php must deregister and optionally (flagged) remove content.
schema_package.gate: schema_build_test in a throwaway Playground is THE safety mechanism, mirroring the block factory: activate, assert each declared post type appears in /wp/v2/types, meta keys appear in the type's REST schema, taxonomies in /wp/v2/taxonomies, each route answers (2xx for a valid sample call, 401/403 for an unauthenticated protected call), binding sources resolve in a probe tree, uninstall leaves no registrations behind. No zip without a green gate; nothing reaches the instance without the zip.

agent_side.packaging: Unchanged: the ONE x-agent plugin, the ONE MCP server. New tools are namespaced wp_schema_*; new skill ships beside wp-blocks.

mcp_tool_additions.name: wp_schema_scaffold
mcp_tool_additions.input: {slug, intent: string, post_types: [{slug, label, supports, meta: [{key, type, schema}], taxonomies?}], routes?: [{path, methods, auth: 'public-nonce'|'capability', capability?}], bindings?: [{name, meta_key}]}
mcp_tool_additions.behavior: Template a schema package; intent embedded as the implementation comment exactly like render_intent.

mcp_tool_additions.name: wp_schema_build_test
mcp_tool_additions.output: {built, smoke: {types_registered, meta_in_rest, routes: [{path, status}], php_error?}, zip_path?}
mcp_tool_additions.behavior: Run the gate above in @wp-playground/cli; structured failure detail; no zip on any failure.

mcp_tool_additions.name: wp_schema_install
mcp_tool_additions.behavior: POST /schema/install; refresh manifest + reload harness to the new epoch; posture-guarded.

mcp_tool_amendments: wp_block_scaffold gains {interactivity: 'none'|'view-script'|'interactivity-api', stylesheet: bool}. 'view-script' templates a vanilla view.js (no framework, no build-time deps beyond wp-scripts) declared as block.json viewScript; 'interactivity-api' templates data-wp-* directives in render.php + a store module, only offered when manifest.features.interactivity_api is true. stylesheet templates style.css restricted to token custom properties.

wp_block_build_test smoke additionally asserts: viewScript enqueues and executes without console errors against the rendered sample; style.css enqueues; any hardcoded color/size literal in style.css (not a var(--wp--preset--*)) is a warning surfaced in the result.
wp_validate implements the three new diagnostics locally where possible (styles, bindable attributes) before the round trip.
agent_side.interactivity_policy: Default rung is 'view-script' vanilla JS for progressive enhancement (submit-over-fetch, toggles, client state that never leaves the page). Escalate to the Interactivity API only when state must flow server->client (hydration, context sharing across blocks) AND manifest.features.interactivity_api is true. Both rungs are canon; React or any framework on the front end is outside canon and forbidden.

new_skill.frontmatter: name + description tuned to trigger on: storage, orders/bookings/submissions/inventory, custom post types, taxonomies, custom fields/meta, block bindings, REST endpoints, admin screens, 'where does the data live', and any block whose behavior needs a backend.
mandatory_rules: S1 Model before UI: post types, taxonomies, meta, and routes are designed and installed BEFORE the blocks that render them. The data model is the source of truth; blocks are views.

S2 Read the model first: wp_manifest section=data_model + bindings at the current fingerprint. Extend what exists (a taxonomy term, a meta key) before registering anything new; registering a parallel model beside an existing one is the schema-side equivalent of hand-written markup.
S3 Everything REST-visible: no meta without show_in_rest schema, no CPT the agent cannot read back through /wp/v2. If the agent can't see it in the manifest afterwards, it doesn't exist.

S4 Bindings over bespoke rendering: when a core block + a binding to registered meta can display the data, that beats a custom block. Cite manifest.bindings before building a rung-3 block that merely displays a field.
S5 The factory gate is not skippable: scaffold -> implement -> wp_schema_build_test green -> wp_schema_install -> adopt the new fingerprint in the very next tree.

S6 Anonymous write flows (order forms, RSVPs) go through a package-registered route with nonce + honeypot + server-side validation; never through comments, options, or transients. Content types the public writes get moderated statuses by design.
S7 A schema package is owned code with an uninstall story. Say the cost out loud when you create one, exactly as R7 rung 3 requires for blocks.
S8 Posture: /schema/install is extend-tier. Production = snapshot -> sandbox -> promote. Never around the wall.
new_skill.worked_example_required: The bakery ordering system rebuilt end-to-end: agent/orders schema package (hc_order CPT with moderated statuses, meta with REST schemas, nonce-guarded submit route, standard admin list) + the order-form block reduced to a styled form with view.js fetch submission + a binding displaying pickup-day on a core block. Literal tool-call transcripts, including the schema_build_test failure path.

wp_blocks_amendments: R4 is superseded by the expression_ladder (referenced, with the citation rule).

R7 gains the handoff rule (rung 3.5): if the gap is storage, backend behavior, or an admin surface — stop climbing the block ladder; that is wp-schema territory. A block may be the VIEW of a schema package, never its database.
R5 gains: blocks with interactivity declare the rung (view-script | interactivity-api) and why; wp_block_build_test's console-error assertion is part of the gate.
New R11: block-owned stylesheets use token custom properties exclusively; a literal hex or px that exists as a token is a defect the build_test warning already names.

progress_protocol.same_as: companion spec progress_protocol — identical file schema and rules; record here the interfaces v2 additivity check and every WP-API surface verified against developer.wordpress.org rather than memory (bindings registry, per-block css, interactivity API).

non_goals: No separate agent-side plugin (decision recorded above; revisit only if a trust story cannot be met by extend-tier gating plus tool allowlists).
No front-end frameworks: view.js is vanilla; the Interactivity API is the only sanctioned stateful escalation.
No direct SQL, no bespoke admin frameworks, no settings pages — the CPT's standard admin UI is the admin surface.

No commerce suite integration in this spec: if a commerce suite is active it appears in the manifest like any vocabulary; installing one remains a product decision made in the prompt, never a factory default.
No relaxation of the base contract: postures, epoch semantics, no-hand-written-markup, and the block factory's dynamic-only rule all stand.
Custom CSS never becomes a first resort: rungs 5 and 6 require the cited failure of rungs 1-4, enforced by skill discipline and surfaced by build_test warnings, not by trusting restraint.
